title: refactor(ci): unify lint/test/release workflows and optimize cache parallelism
author: Lena Park
body: Motivation: Our repository has accumulated multiple overlapping GitHub Actions workflows for linting, unit tests, integration tests, and release automation which cause duplicated configuration, inconsistent caching behavior, and slow CI matrices. This PR consolidates the lint/test/release workflows into a unified routing pattern, standardizes cache keys to reduce cache misses, and reduces parallelism where it was wasteful to improve runner availability. Summary of changes: 1) Replace .github/workflows/{lint.yml, test.yml, release.yml, ci-matrix.yml} with a smaller set: .github/workflows/ci.yml (lint + unit + integration routing), .github/workflows/release.yml (release orchestration simplified), and .github/workflows/workflow-helpers.yml (shared reusable jobs). 2) Introduce consistent cache keys keyed by job-type+node-version+hash(package-lock.json) to reduce miss rate. 3) Reduce default matrix parallelism for integration tests from 6->3 and enable conditional parallelism based on path filters. 4) Consolidate Node toolcache setup and move heavy setup to reusable composite actions to shorten warmup times. 5) Add a lightweight release dry-run job and improve tagging/annotation hygiene. Checklist: - [x] Move common steps into reusable composite actions - [x] Update internal docs and PR templates to reference unified workflows - [x] Run full CI across main branches and validate artifacts - [x] Performance benchmark: averaged CI runtime reduced ~18% on sample branch - [x] Coordinate with release owners for the new release dry-run job Testing performed: All jobs were exercised on a fork and on a dedicated branch; lint and test failures were fixed; a flaky integration test was pinned and added to the quarantine suite; release dry-run executed against staging registry. Rollout plan: This PR is merged with a staged rollout: monitor CI throughput and cache hit rates for 48 hours; revert or tweak parallelism if regressions observed. Related work: Linear ENG-8421 (CI modernization), ENG-9123 (release automation hygiene). Notes: This description is intentionally a single continuous string to match export expectations.
